..
Issued at 1209 PM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

There is currently dry, southwesterly flow aloft over southern 
Idaho. Also, currently there is an upper level low centered just
off the coast of Washington as part of an overall trough that
extends much farther south to off the coast of California, 
where there is ample moisture available. This low/trough will 
drive the weather/precipitation over the upcoming weekend.

We are in-between systems today. Expect dry conditions today 
with temperatures warming a few degrees, compared to yesterday, 
with southwesterly flow aloft. Highs today reach the mid to 
upper 50s for most of us in the lower elevations with more 
cities reaching the upper 50s. Winds will be fairly light today 
with gusts around 15 to 20 mph.

Friday morning look for patchy fog, especially in lower 
elevations near water sources. Expect better fog chances
Saturday and, especially, Sunday and Monday mornings. Friday 
look for slightly warmer temperatures, compared to Thursday, 
with highs in the 50s to near 60s. On Friday, the low currently 
off the Washington coast and the associated trough will gather 
Pacific moisture and eject a weak shortwave through Idaho. Wind 
gusts begin to increase on Friday, closer to 20-30 mph for many.
This will also bring some isolated to scattered showers back to
the Central Mountains as early as Friday morning with coverage 
increasing a bit on Friday afternoon through early Saturday. 
This first "quick" round of precipitation will bring about 0.10 
to 0.20 inches of precipitation the the area which will also 
mean to expect a few inches of snow up on top of the mountains, 
too. Most of this will be above pass level, but there is about a
half inch to an inch of snow in the current forecast for Galena
Summit from Friday morning to Saturday morning. 

Saturday late afternoon into the early evening models still 
show a chance for 0.01 to 0.08 inch of rain across lower 
elevations that will likely have some impacts on Halloween 
activities. However, the bulk of the precipitation is still 
arriving later Saturday evening through Sunday and lingering 
into Monday morning. 

By late Saturday into Sunday the low off the Washington coast 
begins to move and makes it way inland aided by an deepening 
trough, which will really pick up more Pacific moisture and 
transport it over southeastern Idaho. This more organized round 
of precipitation will begin in the Central Mountains/Wood River 
Valley/eastern Magic Valley as early as 6 PM Saturday and then 
spread eastward throughout the night. The NBM model is still 
showing about an 80 to 100 percent chance of the entire CWA 
receiving at least 0.25 inch of precipitation from 5 AM Saturday
to 5 AM Monday. Precipitation amounts have not changed much 
from yesterdays model run. It still seems likely that many will 
see 0.25 to 0.50 inches in the eastern Magic Valley, 0.50 to 
0.75 inches in the Snake River Plain and lower elevations of the
Eastern Highlands and Central Mountains. For higher elevations 
(above 8000 to 85000 feet) precipitation will be pushing 0.80 
to 1.50 inches, especially for Sun Valley Region, Big Lost 
Highlands/Copper Basin, Lost River Range, and the Montana Divide
as well as the Southern areas along the Utah border including 
the Wasatch mountains. Temperatures will still be "warm" on 
Saturday with highs in the 50s, but by Sunday our highs will 
drop into the mid and upper 40s. Snow impacts seem likely at 
Galena Summit Saturday night into Sunday morning with the 
forecast still showing 4-6" of snow there. A winter weather 
advisory for the Sun Valley Region and the Big Lost Highlands 
above 7500 to 8000 feet for Saturday evening through Sunday 
will likely be needed. Elsewhere, the bulk of our snow is 
expected to remain above most of the rest of our mountain 
passes, but that could change easily with temperature changes of
just a few degrees. Even though snow levels will start high, 
convection can lower snow levels, which could drop snow levels 
to pass levels especially for areas like Emigration and Raynolds
pass. 

A few showers linger on Monday morning, but we will be drying out 
from west to east by that point and high pressure builds in over the 
area through mid week.
